# Clarified Acceptance Requirements Checklist: X/Twitter Media Download

**Purpose**: Review whether the clarified URL, delivery-scope, deadline, size-limit, and duplicate-request decisions are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and measurable
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) and [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the $speckit-checklist command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item [x] only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: [x] means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Clarification Traceability

- [ ] CHK001 Does each clarification answer have a corresponding, non-contradictory requirement or acceptance scenario rather than existing only in the session log? [Traceability, Spec §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the five clarified decisions explicitly reflected in the assumptions and scope boundaries so later planning cannot silently revert them? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the terms “directly deliverable,” “partial-result summary,” “duplicate delivery,” and “Telegram cloud upload ceiling” defined well enough for independent reviewers to interpret them consistently? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010–FR-021]

## URL Allowlist Quality

- [ ] CHK004 Does the URL requirement specify the complete accepted hostname set, including whether x.com, twitter.com, and their optional www forms are case-normalized consistently? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the required status-path shape clear about account-segment syntax, numeric post-ID bounds, trailing slashes, extra path segments, and encoded path characters? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK006 Are query and fragment handling requirements clear about whether they are ignored only for validation, removed from the canonical reference, or also excluded from provider/error reporting? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK007 Are rejected mobile hosts, short links, HTTP schemes, credentials, and non-default ports consistently classified across the invalid-input acceptance scenarios and edge cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002–FR-003]
- [ ] CHK008 Does the redirect requirement distinguish an accepted original URL from a rejected redirect destination without implying that rejected short links become valid through redirection? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Direct-Delivery Scope

- [ ] CHK009 Do all video and animation acceptance scenarios consistently state that incompatible media fails safely rather than being transformed in the MVP? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 1, Spec §User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK010 Is “directly deliverable representation” defined in terms of supported media kind, container/codec, size, and Telegram send constraints? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the boundary between “no supported media,” “no compatible representation,” processing failure, and delivery failure explicit enough to produce distinct user outcomes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK012 Does the future transformation allowance preserve the stated MVP exclusion without weakening the requirement that future support must not change the user-facing X/Twitter workflow? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK013 Are animated GIF representations and playable direct-delivery formats described consistently so “animated media” does not imply a transformation requirement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §User Story 2]

## Deadline and Partial-Outcome Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Does the specification distinguish an item that failed after being attempted from an item that was never attempted because the job deadline or cancellation arrived? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK015 Are partial-result summaries required to preserve delivered items and identify unattempted positions as timed out or cancelled without exposing internal diagnostics? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK016 Are deadline/cancellation semantics consistent for extraction, downloading, delivery, and a multi-item post where the deadline arrives between items? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the outcome defined when a deadline arrives before any item is delivered, including whether the result is a timeout, total failure, or rejected request? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-015]

## Size and Resource Acceptance

- [ ] CHK018 Is 49 MiB defined unambiguously as the default per-item byte limit, including the unit conversion and whether the limit applies to downloaded bytes, prepared bytes, or both? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the rule that configuration may lower but never raise the limit stated consistently with the delivery-limit assumption and user-facing too-large outcome? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-015, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 Does the specification define how a representation whose size is unknown or whose declared size is inaccurate is treated under the hard per-item limit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK021 Are the success criteria’s “within supported delivery limits” and “deliverable supported item” terms aligned with the clarified 49 MiB and direct-delivery rules? [Traceability, Spec §SC-001–SC-002]

## Duplicate and Concurrency Semantics

- [ ] CHK022 Does the no-deduplication requirement clearly apply to duplicate Telegram updates, manual resubmissions, concurrent identical URLs, and process restarts? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the acceptance of duplicate deliveries consistent with the requirement that no result crosses into another originating chat? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017–FR-018, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK024 Are resource bounds and user feedback defined for duplicate requests that collectively saturate the active/queued capacity? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-017–FR-021]

## Plan and Spec Alignment

- [ ] CHK025 Does the technical plan’s accepted URL list reject mobile hosts, short links, HTTP, credentials, and non-default ports exactly as the clarified specification requires? [Conflict, Spec §FR-002, Plan §X provider and process]
- [ ] CHK026 Does the technical plan’s direct-MP4/no-FFmpeg decision match the clarified direct-delivery-only MVP acceptance criteria? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Plan §Media processing]
- [ ] CHK027 Does the technical plan use the clarified 49 MiB ceiling and preserve the rule that deployment configuration may only lower it? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, Plan §Configuration and Operations]
- [ ] CHK028 Does the technical plan’s duplicate-request behavior remain stateless and independent, without introducing an unapproved cache or persistence mechanism? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, Plan §Concurrency and Resource Ownership]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK029 Can SC-001 distinguish a directly deliverable item from an item that is supported by X but intentionally outside the MVP’s processing scope? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK030 Does SC-005’s 100-request mixed test explicitly include duplicate submissions, deadline-partial outcomes, direct-delivery failures, and the 49 MiB boundary? [Completeness, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK031 Are the timing targets in SC-002 and SC-003 defined against the clarified job deadline and input-validation behavior rather than an unspecified “normal” environment? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002–SC-003]
- [ ] CHK032 Does SC-004 cover safe user outcomes for no-compatible-representation, too-large, cancelled-partial, and duplicate-request scenarios introduced by clarification? [Coverage, Spec §SC-004, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-021]

## Notes

- Mark items [x] only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- $speckit-implement reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- checklists/requirements.md has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by $speckit-specify and $speckit-clarify
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
